title: Interview: dev tooling and conventions
lead: Settle the development conventions every later slice assumes.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** writing any code; the skeleton itself (next slice).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Every implementation slice names test commands, file paths and dependency rules. If they are not settled first, those slices are built on guesses.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
1. Minimum Python version? Recommend the newest version available on the deployment host and in the container base image (≥3.11 needed for `tomllib`).
2. Test runner: stdlib `unittest` (recommended, no dependency) or pytest (dependency)?
3. Lint/format: none, or a tool such as ruff (dependency, needs approval)?
4. Dependency pinning: `requirements.txt` with exact pins and hashes (recommended), or a lock tool (dependency)?
5. Layout: `src/larder/` package + `tests/` (recommended) or flat?
6. Type hints: required on public functions? Run a type checker (dependency)?
7. Commit message convention for this repo?

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `local/` private notes (not committed)
- `docs/decisions/0017-dev-conventions.md` (new)
- Dependent slices (via `slicer edit`)

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Ask the Owner input questions with options and a recommendation; batch them.
2. Record the answers in the owner's private notes (`local/`, not committed) and an ADR `0017-dev-conventions.md`.
3. Update the "Project skeleton and AGENTS.md" slice's Implement/Check with the chosen commands (`slicer edit`).
4. If a test runner other than unittest is chosen, update the Failing tests wording in the open slices.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- ADR 0017 exists and is linked from README.
- Raw answers are recorded in `local/`; nothing household-specific is committed.
- `slicer show` on "Project skeleton and AGENTS.md" shows concrete commands.
- `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
